stem:
A student investigates the discharge of capacitors in the circuit shown in Fig. 2.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The capacitors have capacitances *C*ₐ and *C*ᵦ.

The student closes the switch to charge the capacitors.

The switch is opened and a stop-watch is started. The capacitors discharge through the resistor of resistance *R*. At a fixed time *t* the voltmeter reading *V* is recorded.

The experiment is repeated for different values of *C*ₐ and *C*ᵦ.

For each combination of *C*ₐ and *C*ᵦ, the combined capacitance *C* is calculated.

It is suggested that *C* and *V* are related by the equation

*V* = *I*₀*R* $e^{- rac{t}{CR}}$

where *I*₀ is the initial current in the resistor.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A graph is plotted of ln *V* on the *y*-axis against $\frac{1}{C}$ on the *x*-axis.

Determine expressions for the gradient and *y*-intercept.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Values of *C*ₐ, *C*ᵦ and *V* are given in Table 2.1.

[[fig:f2]]

The relationship between *C*, *C*ₐ and *C*ᵦ is

$\frac{1}{C} = \frac{C_A + C_B}{C_A C_B}$.

Calculate and record values of $\frac{1}{C} / 10^4\,\mathrm{F}^{-1}$ and ln (*V* / V) in Table 2.1.

Include the absolute uncertainties in ln (*V* / V).

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Plot a graph of ln (*V* / V) against $\frac{1}{C} / 10^4\,\mathrm{F}^{-1}$.

Include error bars for ln (*V* / V).

[[fig:f3]]

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Draw the straight line of best fit and a worst acceptable straight line on your graph. Label both lines.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Determine the gradient of the line of best fit. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text: Determine the *y*-intercept of the line of best fit. Do not include the absolute uncertainty.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text:
Using your answers to (a), (c)(iii) and (c)(iv), determine the values of *R* and *I*₀. Include appropriate units.

Data: *t* = (30 ± 1) s

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the percentage uncertainty in R̄.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text: The experiment is repeated with the same value of *t*. Determine the combined capacitance *C* that gives a value of *V* of 1.20V.

figures.caption: Fig. 2.1
figures.alt: Circuit with a switch, two capacitors Cₐ and Cᵦ in series, a voltmeter across them, and a resistor in a parallel branch.

figures.caption: Table 2.1
figures.alt: Table with columns for Cₐ, Cᵦ, 1/C, V/V and ln (V/V), containing six rows of capacitor values and voltage readings.
Blank graph grid with ln (V/V) on the vertical axis and 1/C / 10⁴ F⁻¹ on the horizontal axis.

notes: The line introducing the capacitors appears to read “The capacitors have capacitances Cₐ and Cᵦ.”
problems: part d-i: numeric part needs answer {symbol, unit} (either may be null)
